text:
nina: Heads-up: customers hitting weird typing + runtime import issues when using the JS SDK in edge bundles. Gen types become `any` after esbuild and some imports fail with `is not a function`. Repro in a minimal sample.
rahul: can you paste the tiny repro and tsconfig so we can triage?
nina: sure — handler and tsconfig below. compressed repro: \n```ts
// samples/edge-mini/src/handler.ts
import RedwoodClient from '@redwood/inference'
const c = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })
export default async function (req: Request) {
  const res = await c.generate<{ text: string }>({ prompt: 'hey' })
  // editor shows { text: string } but after bundle res looks like any / missing props
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(res))
}
```
tsconfig used by the sample: \n```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2020",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "declaration": true,
    "esModuleInterop": false
  }
}
```
nina: bundle log: "warning: Could not parse declaration files emitted by TypeScript. Falling back to any." then deployed edge route throws: `TypeError: RedwoodClient is not a function`.
marc: two separate signals: (1) overload-heavy .d.ts shapes can confuse isolatedModules and bundlers; (2) publish-time interop between CJS/ESM means default vs named import changes depending on consumer flags.
anya: short-term mitigation: update samples to recommend `esModuleInterop: true` or `module: 'NodeNext'` for Node-edge runtimes, and document the caveat. Long-term: make the exported typings resilient.
rahul: proposal: collapse outward-facing overloads into one well-typed generic signature so inference doesn't depend on overload order. Example: `generate<T = string | Record<string, unknown>>(opts: GenerateOptions): Promise<T>`. Keep internal overload helpers but don't publish them as top-level exports.
marc: also ensure package.json `types` points to a single `dist/index.d.ts` entry and add a tiny `types/compat.d.ts` that maps older overload names for legacy consumers. That reduces ambiguous deep import picks.
anya: CI change: add a matrix run that does `tsc --noEmit --project samples/edge-mini` with `isolatedModules` and an esbuild bundle step (`esbuild src/handler.ts --bundle --platform=browser --format=esm`) and a simple node import smoke test for CJS/ESM. Block on type/bundle failures.
nina: CI already failed for my branch: https://ci.internal/redsdk/4492 — typecheck + bundle warnings. build-bot flagged errors and assigned @anya.
build-bot: Build failed — see https://ci.internal/redsdk/4492 (typecheck, bundle). @anya assigned.
rahul: plan for the PR: (A) replace public overloads with single generic signatures; (B) publish `types` shim and compatibility helpers; (C) update sample tsconfig and add a README note; (D) add CI matrix; (E) add a short migration blurb in RELEASE_NOTES.
anya: i'll open PR #3042 with those changes and include a runnable sample under `samples/edge-mini` so external contributors can test locally.
marc: after PR merge, run smoke checks against a couple internal routes that use deep generics so we catch runtime surprises. I'll queue that.
nina: thanks — this should reduce onboarding friction and support load. :thumbsup:
rahul: also add a quick GH issue template for SDK typing regressions so new reports include tsconfig, bundler, and a tiny repro by default. saves triage time.
anya: PR opened #3042 — tagging @marc @rahul for review. I'll follow up with the sample README and CHANGELOG note.
nina: awesome, appreciate the quick turnaround.
